title: fix(app-shell): the dataset-filter read half opens a stored condition only when the builder can hold it (objectui#10257)
body:
Fixes #10257

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`conditionToGroup` (the read half of the Studio dataset-filter bridge) opened two kinds of stored condition as editable rows that the builder cannot hold. `DatasetFilterField.commitFilterGroup` saves on every change, so an edit to a SIBLING row rewrote or dropped them:

1. **Incomplete stored values** (the card): `{ $eq: '' }` and `{ $in: [] }`, plus the rest of the class (`$ne: ''`, `$nin: []`, a `null` comparand, and the implicit `{ field: '' }` / `{ field: null }` / `{ field: [] }`). The read half returned `representable: true`, and `groupToCondition` drops these as unfinished rows. I re-measured this on the branch base `747f3347d`: `conditionToGroup({ $and: [{ stage: { $eq: 'won' } }, { name: { $eq: '' } }] })` is representable, and editing `stage` commits `{ stage: { $eq: 'lost' } }`.
2. **Operators the column's bucket does not offer** (seat 1's addendum, comment 5817965568): `$in` on a date column, `$gt` on a text column, `$in` on a number column. Generalised to every token, this also covers `$exists` / `$null` on a boolean column. The panel drew a blank operator trigger, and `reconcileOperatorForField` gives `equals`.

## The direction: the read half refuses, for both classes

This applies objectui#10062's read-half `$between` guard (PR #10253) to every token. objectui#9363 and objectui#9372 made the write half CARRY a shape only where a finished builder row means exactly that spec predicate. A shape the write half could not carry faithfully stayed out of the builder: it was dropped inertly, or its stored form read back as non-representable. Neither class here can be carried by the write half:

- `equals ''` is also the row the builder SEEDS on "Add condition". A write half that kept `{ $eq: '' }` would emit a filter for every unfinished row. That is the silently-wrong filter its incomplete-row drop exists to prevent.
- The bucket gap happens in the panel, before anything reaches the bridge, so the write half has nothing to keep.

So one shape gets one answer from both halves: the row is refused, and the Source tab takes the filter.

## What changed

- There is a new `builderHolds(row, fields)` in `datasetFilterCondition.ts`. `conditionToGroup` calls it on every read-back row, from every arm: `$exists`, `$null`, the `$`-operator arm and implicit equality. Any `false` gives `representable: false`. It checks two things:
  1. **Would the write half keep the row?** It asks `groupToCondition` itself, not a copy of its rules, so the halves cannot drift apart. This refuses an incomplete value. It also refuses a stored condition keyed by an empty field name, which the write half drops for the same reason.
  2. **Does the column's bucket offer the row's operator?** Checked only when a field list is given, through `operatorsForFieldType(type)`. That is the same bucket function, called the same way (no opt-ins), that the builder uses for each row and that `readBackOperator` already reads. No second operator table. A column listed without a type, or not listed at all, gets the text bucket the builder draws for it, as the `$between` rule already did.
- The pair-only `$between` block is removed because `builderHolds` covers it. The four objectui#10062 `$between` pins pass unchanged, and they now go red when `builderHolds` is ablated.
- `groupToCondition` (the write half) is byte-identical. The one-time probe below compares its source text.
- In `datasetFilterCondition.dateRoundTrip-9382.test.tsx`, one leg is inverted. It expected `{ mystery: { $gt: 1 } }` on an unlisted column to read back as `greaterThan`. The builder draws the text bucket for an unlisted column, which lacks `greaterThan`, so that read now refuses. A new control shows that an unlisted `$eq` still reads back as `equals`.

## PM mechanism assumptions, measured

- **A1 holds.** The generalisation reuses `operatorsForFieldType` with no extras. `FilterBuilder.getOperatorsForField` calls that function, and the `$between` rule and `readBackOperator` already read it.
- **A2 holds.** I ran a one-time probe comparing the old bridge (`747f3347d`) with the new one over 7980 reads.
  - Inputs: 210 stored shapes, each alone and beside a finished row. Each was read with no field list, with the column unlisted, with an empty list, and listed under each of 16 column-type values (including no type and an unknown type).
  - 3418 reads give byte-identical answers. The other 4562 all went from representable to non-representable. Each one is explained: 714 incomplete values, 3080 operators off the column's bucket, 768 both. 0 are unexplained.
  - The write half's source text is identical.
  - The new test adds a permanent byte-identity leg. Every row the dropdown can build, filled in, reopens as itself and writes back byte-identical, across all 14 inspector bucket types.
- **A3 is partly falsified.** "Field-less reads unchanged" holds: a read with NO field list skips the bucket check, as the addendum says. The addendum's "field-less" matches the `$between` comment's "Only a read with NO field list skips this".
  - A condition whose field is NOT IN the list does change. `FilterBuilder` draws such a row with `operatorsForFieldType(undefined)`, the text bucket, and the `$between` precedent already refuses it. The pin: "a column listed WITHOUT a type, or not listed at all ... not representable". One rule for every token therefore refuses an unlisted `$in` / `$gt` too.
  - A token the text bucket offers (`$eq`, `$contains`, and so on) on an unlisted column is unchanged. I followed the ruling's "generalise the `$between` rule to every token" over the assumption's reading.

## Evidence (head `7543da0bd`)

- **Red-first.** I ran the new test file on the unmodified tree: `Tests 14 failed | 11 passed (25)`. The failures were exactly the predicted legs:
  - every `representable: false` pin;
  - the swept invariant, which listed 924 broken entries covering both classes;
  - the three real-inspector refusals.

  The WHY, CONTROL, reachable, builder-domain and field-less legs were green.
- **Reverse proof.** The fix was committed first. Then objectstack's `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` removed the single `builderHolds` call in `conditionToGroup`. The anchor hit once, went from 1 to 0, and the blob changed from `5037f5c55a4d` to `927bf20ec8cb`.
  - Result over the new file and the 9382 file: `Tests 19 failed | 33 passed (52)`. The 19 are the 14 new pins, the inverted 9382 leg, and the four `$between` precedent pins.
  - Restore verified: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
  - No dist build was involved, because the tests import the bridge by relative path.
- **Targeted tests at `7543da0bd`:** the new file, the four existing `datasetFilterCondition*` suites and the three `DatasetDefaultInspector*` suites. Result: `Test Files 8 passed (8)`, `Tests 125 passed (125)`.
- **Build and type-check.** The closure build `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` exited 0. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0. `--listFiles` on `tsconfig.test.json` lists the new test, the 9382 test and the bridge, once each.
- **Lint, narrowed to the 3 touched files, as a measurement:**
  1. Population: app-shell's `lint` is `eslint .` under the root `eslint.config.js`. There is no package-local config.
  2. `--format json` counts 3 files, 0 errors and 3 `no-explicit-any` warnings. All three warnings are on the two `as any` lines that were already there; the base file has the same count.
  3. The config enables no type-aware linting (no `projectService` or `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot change a verdict on an untouched file.
- **Gates**, all exit 0 at `7543da0bd`: `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:self-import`, `check-lint-coverage`.
- **Source-text anchor pins:** `git grep` finds no test or script that quotes the lines this diff changes.

## REWORK round 1 (head `f3de6d54f`)

The contract review passed on the code. The seat's comment 5825731886 on objectui#10257 amended the claim's file surface to add `.changeset/9382-dataset-filter-date-operator-round-trip.md`, body only. One commit, `f3de6d54f`, touches that file and nothing else: `git diff --name-only 7543da0bd f3de6d54f` lists only it. So the source, the tests, and every code measurement above are unchanged.

- **The false sentence.** It said an ambiguous `$gt` / `$lt` the column cannot settle "falls back to the unchanged fixed table". With a field list, which the inspector always passes, `builderHolds` now refuses that row and sends the filter to the Source tab. The paragraph now says so. It adds that, with a field list, the refusal covers all three cases it lists. An untyped or unlisted column gets the text menu, which offers neither `greaterThan` nor `lessThan`. A menu offering neither candidate cannot offer the fallback, since the fallback is one of them. Only a read with no field list still opens the row under the fixed-table operator.
- **Measured at head** with a one-time probe (deleted). With no field list, `$gt` and `$lt` open as `greaterThan` / `lessThan`. With a field list they are refused when the column is untyped, when it is unlisted, and under each of `text`, `boolean`, `select`, `status`, `lookup`, `master_detail`, `user` and an unknown type; all eight offer neither candidate.
- **Frontmatter byte-identical.** The sha256 of the frontmatter block is `d5a45968c712fcbb04974d23f5e3a6a19e3a6dc646176d2d6034bab8f1d93a54` at both `7543da0bd` and `f3de6d54f`.
- **The rest of the file**, re-read against head, is left alone.
  - The "6 broke, the other 116" figures are a dated measurement of the pre-objectui#9382 tree, not a claim about head.
  - "The write half is unchanged" and "`@object-ui/components` is untouched" still hold with this PR applied.
- **Gates at `f3de6d54f`**, all exit 0:
  - `check-changeset-presence`;
  - `check:changeset-claims`: 2 changesets in the self-contradiction corpus, both clean, and "No pending changeset names a file this change touches";
  - `check-changeset-no-major`;
  - `check-changeset-overwrite`: report-only, case 2, "declared at base: @object-ui/app-shell: patch" and "declares now: @object-ui/app-shell: patch";
  - `check:control-bytes`;
  - `check:new-line-citations`: 0 new.
- Not changed, as the seat directed: the "Advanced filter (nested / OR)" note in `DatasetDefaultInspector.tsx`.

## Acceptance notes

- **An empty field list (loading).** `DatasetDefaultInspector` builds the filter columns from `useDatasetFieldCatalog`. Its `fieldOptions` is `[]` until the base object loads, and stays `[]` if the load fails.
  - Under the precedent's rule an empty list is still a list. So during that window, a filter whose operator the text bucket lacks (for example `$in` on a select column) shows the Source-tab note instead of the "N conditions" trigger.
  - With `[]` the popover draws no builder in either case: it shows "Pick a base object to add filter conditions." Nothing is written in either state.
  - `$between` has behaved this way since objectui#10062. The changeset says so. The seat ruled to keep it (Q1 A, comment 5825731886).
- The Source-tab note reads "Advanced filter (nested / OR)". It now also covers incomplete values and off-bucket operators, as it already did for `$between`. `DatasetDefaultInspector.tsx` is outside this claim's file surface, so I left the wording alone.
- The pending objectui#9382 changeset's fallback sentence is corrected in place (see REWORK round 1 above), so it stays true when both changesets publish together.
- This is a dispatched draft and stays draft. Marking it ready and queueing it belong to the dispatching seat.
